html:
Activity, progress and execution visualization

The controller emits trace/activity events as the run progresses. The browser projects these into activity rows, tool detail, progress narration, timing and execution diagrams. A row is a view of server state; selecting it cannot confer scheduler or completion authority.

Console data and lifecycle flows trace the independent diagnostic sidecar, its cached observations, local GPU readings and explicit stack capture. Diagnostic findings do not establish task completion.

Trace ownership and read paths

AgentTraceStore publishes request headers and events through the TraceJournal facade. A Controller-owned path selects MemoryTraceJournal: live reads and writes use the state hub, while recovery and checkpoints use the versioned SQLite representation. An unowned path retains the standalone SQLite adapter used by compatibility callers and fixtures. See Controller state and recovery for checkpoint ownership.

flowchart LR E[Published trace events] --> T[AgentTraceStore] T --> J[TraceJournal facade] J --> R[Controller RAM records and indexes] R --> C[Checkpoint generation] R --> H[Compact header and timing reads] R --> W[Cursor event windows] W --> P[Activity preview projection] R --> D[Explicit retained detail]

The journal stores headers separately from immutable event pages. Request headers exclude events and raw_payloads; event privacy filtering belongs to the publication path. Capability identities deduplicate replay. Disabled-check observation lookups retain their first matching event. Deleting a live request publishes a tombstone with the deletion, so delayed writes cannot recreate it; the event sequence continues rather than reusing old IDs.

Routine status, timing and answer reads copy only their needed fields. Cursor windows combine a header and ordered events from one retained revision. Event IDs are global, so loading progress counts this request's earlier events rather than subtracting IDs. Changed trace generations reset stale cursors. The store bounds each delta page to 100 events; callers needing exact detail use its retained event identity. Neither reading nor reopening a page repairs or reexecutes work.

Default full-trace restoration selects the last 5,000 events plus every retained capability event and conversation.message. It can therefore exceed 5,000 rows. This selection is not a journal deletion policy. Only explicitly expired timeline diagnostics are retired through the diagnostic-expiry path; conversation deletion and retention remain separate lifecycle operations.

activity_page.py projects these windows into previews. Compact mode groups only explicitly cumulative receiving-progress records for the same call, operation and phase. Exact mode disables that grouping and preserves the selected event sequence; redaction and preview shortening still apply. Inspector links lead to retained detail. Paging cursors come from scanned events, including rows omitted from the compact view, so grouping does not skip retained history.

conversation_delivery.py keeps explicit user/assistant text and marked public answer streams when private diagnostics are removed. It does not reconstruct chat from tool output or private reasoning. completion_report.py records factual runtime completion messages when needed, with stable identities per resumption epoch. Existing answers, explicit silence and nonterminal waits keep their contracts. A report says no commands were sent only when preflight evidence explicitly proves nonexecution and excludes unknown effects.

Operation headings use operation_preview.py. Control removal and shortening always apply; credential masking follows the selected optional source policy. URL labels do not unconditionally remove query, fragment or user information. Review the redaction settings before sharing previews or retained detail.

The isolated journal parity tests check SQL/RAM projections, recovery, tombstones and live reads without SQLite. Activity-page fixtures check pagination, Unicode byte bounds, cumulative grouping and retained command context without running the commands shown in the evidence.

Runtime notices and retained execution evidence

Runtime notices describe a problem and its observed recovery. They are separate from agent answers and terminal completion reports. runtime_issues.py groups events by request, subsystem owner, operation/correlation and problem code. Each notice has a stable identity and increasing revision. Replaying the same source event does not count another occurrence; repeated distinct failures can.

A retry updates the correlated unresolved notice. Resolution requires evidence from the same owning subsystem for the affected operation, or an explicit issue identity acknowledged by that owner. Successful completion of the parent task does not prove that a failed child recovered. Ordinary queue/wait states and intentional cancellation do not automatically become failures. Unknown effects retain guidance to reconcile the outcome before deciding whether to retry.

Notice copy comes from catalog definitions, parameter diagnostics or factual execution evidence. It is not a model-generated interpretation of arbitrary exception text. runtime_issue_evidence.py joins only the issue's operation and explicitly linked parallel children. It shows at most 16 selected failed operations, with omitted counts, commands bounded to 4,000 characters and output bounded to 2,000 characters per operation. Child counts describe observed child states; missing facts stay unknown. Exit code, nonexecution and stderr/combined/unavailable output remain distinct.

These error details use mandatory error-catalog sanitization, including known credential and control-character filtering, independently of optional Activity or TRACES masking. Original execution receipts retain their owner. Inspection reads retained request-scoped evidence; it does not poll a Gateway, infer a cause from output text, run a model or authorize recovery.

Command and file context

execution_activity.py joins compact command, invocation, transfer and output-time facts for one operation. An older command-start event can supply a preview even when it is outside the current Activity page. The exact-detail link retains that event identity. execution_context.py shows at most 20 file entries selected from public arguments/results. Requested and Named in command describe intent; observed result/revision evidence is needed for labels such as Created or Written. No path is opened and no shell expression is evaluated to produce these labels.

The Shell event reducer and background-job projection keep process state and output availability separate:

Observation Meaning
Completed with an exit code The process has terminal evidence; a nonzero exit code can still indicate failure.
Output is pending The background capture has not ended; silence does not establish exit.
Output is partial or unavailable Retention/truncation or missing capture limits what can be inspected. It does not establish success or failure by itself.
Output was purged The projection suppresses stale receipt text even if an older copy still exists in supplied data.
Detached or unknown outcome Ending an observer/capture does not prove the remote process stopped. Inspect existing evidence before repeating work.

The background projection applies current TRACES policy before retaining its default tail of 262,144 characters. This is a presentation character limit, not a byte limit or the total stored-log retention policy. Explicit full reads can request all retained text. Neither projection changes command lifetime.

Retained chat messages

display_messages.py records already-published prose before trace persistence and broadcast. Stable message identities and revisions let clients merge updates; monotonically sequenced fragments avoid replay duplicates. Interrupted drafts remain visible as incomplete. A matching accepted answer can supersede its own preview while preserving the earlier record, and later user turns retain prior answers. Message visibility is independent of execution acceptance: visible text alone does not prove a tool ran or a completion requirement passed.

Older traces can lack explicit question/reply events. conversation_history.py repairs only the returned presentation using accepted native ask_user receipts, journal exchanges and steering amendments. It matches questions to recorded waits, places answers at resume boundaries and marks borrowed timestamps as inferred. It uses the existing RAM owner or an existing read-only legacy database; unavailable legacy data leaves saved chat readable. It skips private-content traces and never writes recovered display events into the execution journal.

Runtime notice tests, evidence tests and display-message tests exercise correlation, replay, recovery and privacy with isolated retained state. Command inspection tests use synthetic jobs and receipts; the commands shown by those fixtures are not run.

Reading execution activity

Activity Trace is the history of what happened during a task. Open it to see which tools ran, which computer they used, the information they received, and what they returned. A tool finishing successfully does not prove the whole request was answered correctly. Check the final result too.

Check tool access and approvals

The history shows when tools were selected, enabled, blocked, or approved. These are different steps. Knowing that a tool exists does not mean it ran. Allowing a tool does not approve every action it could take. When approved access lets a task continue, the other restrictions still apply.

Read output without stopping the work

For a command, opening the output only shows what it has returned. Closing that view or your browser tab does not cancel the command. No new output means only that nothing new has arrived; it does not prove the work finished.

Check the recorded result to see whether the command completed or failed. If an action may have made a change but its final result is missing, find out what happened before repeating it.

Follow work that is still running

Open Monitoring activity to see the action being watched. When available, it shows the selected computer, folder, and a short command preview. Each dated update explains the reported status. Actions running at the same time keep their own details.

If the command's start is outside the visible history, opening the details can retrieve its saved information. This does not ask the AI to do more work or run the command again. Older or incomplete records may say that some details are unavailable. The same recorded actions can be viewed on desktop, mobile, or after reopening the conversation.

Understand what the history can show

The amount of detail depends on what your settings keep and display. Looking at the history does not change permissions. The AI output view can only show fields the provider sent and SMTO retained; it cannot reveal private internal reasoning. SMTO checks saved tool results when deciding whether work is complete, rather than relying only on what is visible in the browser.

Settings that hide sensitive information do not cover every kind of output. Review records before sharing them. Commands, user content, or account details may still contain private information.

Private tool diagnostics do not hide the conversation itself. Opening plans, progress messages, and final answers remain visible during execution and after reopening the conversation. An opening overview, when provided, is labeled Agent plan. If the model omits it, execution continues without an opening message. Diagnostic logs omit private tool payloads and raw model responses; chat delivery retains only fields explicitly published for the user, with the configured credential redaction still applied. A missing final answer produces a factual runtime completion report without copying tool content or making another model call.

Model-call latency

In Inspect execution, open Model call overlap to compare concurrent calls. Open a Model call timeline event to inspect preparation, token measurement, capacity waits, transport and response milestones. Calls discarded after steering are labeled separately from accepted decisions. Acceptance of a model response does not authorize a tool operation.

Waiting for controller capacity means the run is waiting for an agent-turn lease. Waiting for model capacity means the existing inference gate has not admitted the call. Job, event, approval and resource waits retain their own status.

Unknown timing stays Unknown. The first SSE event, first observable reasoning and first useful answer/tool characters are different milestones. Time before useful output is not a measurement of provider prefill. Provider queue/prefill durations appear only when supported numerical telemetry is available. Overlapping spans and calls are never summed as elapsed time; separate process clocks stay separate.

Settings → Detailed latency diagnostics controls new tasks. The default is on; accepted, queued and resumed tasks retain their saved value. Turning it off disables the additional call timeline while ordinary activity remains available. Existing checkpoints without the field use the documented default. The view retains up to 64 recent call records, with at most 96 spans each; incomplete records remain incomplete.

Diagnostics do not change model, reasoning, context, cache, concurrency, tool-result mode or permission policy. They contain numerical facts and correlation identities, not additional copies of prompts, reasoning or tool output.

Capability lifecycle

Automatic capability awareness, selection, activation and grants appear as first-class Activity rows on desktop and mobile. Labels and bounded detail use the shared capability presentation contract. The lifecycle includes:

  • Manifest availability and initial selection started/completed/degraded/changed.
  • Agent capability requests, activation, already-active no-ops, blocks and missing setup or authentication after activation.
  • Grant required/prompted, allowed/denied/unclear answers, committed/conflicting settings, and parent/child authority continuation identities.

native_capability_events is an additive durable outbox keyed by (run_id, event_key). The native checkpoint and its events commit in the same writer transaction. Discovery operation IDs, selection IDs and grant IDs make retries idempotent. The bounded native state.events list remains a debugging view; it is not the complete audit history. The AgentTrace journal projects the outbox with a unique capability_event_id, preserving capability history beyond the ordinary recent-event window. Execution and continuation delivery repair missing outbox delivery without repeating execution or duplicating Activity rows. Trace GET and refresh never repair durable state.

Capability details contain allowlisted IDs, epochs, digests, revisions, reason codes and lineage. They exclude arbitrary model rationale, tool output, user answer text, prompts, credentials and configuration values. Durable event delivery uses the existing trace and native continuation paths; it adds no model calls or background polling loop. Conversation snapshots preserve these safe details and child lineage so the grant and continued task remain visible after reload. Diagnostic retention deletes the outbox with the native run. Older traces without capability events retain their existing presentation.

Historical recovery publishes classifier/resource revisions and events for automatic repair, baseline decisions and exact candidate continuation. The dedicated desktop and mobile decision shows selected blocker facts without foreign command text, environment values or logs. Backend eligibility controls the baseline action; a stale decision refreshes the current facts. Baseline acceptance never presents an unknown historical operation as successful or failed.

Tool details expose bounded invocation input and output. LOGS, EVENTS, TRACES and ACTIVITY independently control optional projection at their consumer boundaries. Completion uses raw receipts. Structural reasoning exclusions and size limits apply independently. See Redaction.

Shell output continues to be captured by the existing runtime/Gateway execution path and retained in AgentTraceStore. Normal conversation trace GET/SSE carries command lifecycle and compact metadata, not stdout/stderr transcript chunks; it does not delete the retained evidence. Full raw records keep their separate explicit inspection route. Expanding a captured Shell row opens a read-only, request/operation-scoped command SSE at /api/agent/trace/{request_id}/commands/{operation_id}/stream. It replays retained events and waits on the trace condition for new events. Reconnect uses the trace cursor and generation; every inspected event advances the server cursor, including filtered events.

Collapsing the row closes only that observer stream. Viewing, copying and reconnecting never invoke an LLM, execute a command, poll the Gateway or change command lifetime. Copy output reads the complete retained command transcript on demand, independently of the bounded browser preview. Tool section copy actions likewise use the retained public section data before display truncation, with the same redaction policy. Conversation history retains full final responses so response and code-block copying continue to include the complete answer after reopening a chat. Browser connection state is separate from process state; silence means only that no output has arrived. Completion and exit codes come from receipts. Detached capture and missing final receipts are reported explicitly. Server-side projection through the existing TRACES redaction policy precedes browser delivery; this preserves the current optional redaction contract described above, including literal visibility when disabled.

Each native model call has an Inspect model output disclosure in Activity on desktop and mobile. It replays retained provider-emitted reasoning, answer text and tool-call fragments and follows new output while open. Channel filtering, Copy output and Download full capture support debugging, including calls that failed at their output limit. The download includes call identity, timing, actual request limits, provider usage when available, and finish reason. Character counts are not presented as token counts.

Capture runs independently of the viewer. Text belongs to a separate request/call repository selected by ModelOutputStore: Controller-owned paths use RAM and checkpoint durability; standalone unowned paths use the SQLite compatibility adapter. Its recovery path is <trace-journal-path>.model-output. See the current model observation guide for capture batching, retention and recovery. Ordinary trace/history responses contain no captured text. The browser retains only a 256 Ki-character preview and clearly reports omitted earlier text; copying includes all retained text for the selected channel, and the download includes the full retained capture. Closing the disclosure or hiding the page disconnects inspection without stopping generation or capture. Replay resumes by chunk sequence.

The TRACES redaction setting applies when text is captured, including credentials split across provider fragments. Captured output never becomes executable conversation history, accepted completion evidence, or a tool call. Only fields actually emitted by the provider can be inspected; earlier uncaptured calls and provider-private reasoning cannot be recovered. Restarted captures without a live owner are marked interrupted. Explicit Delete diagnostics and Delete everything remove the conversation's model captures; deleting only the UI chat preserves diagnostic evidence under the existing retention policy.

Progress narration describes ongoing work. Model timing measures request/response transport and generation; it does not measure internal reasoning. Tool timing uses available operation/process receipts. Compaction events report context projection changes. Execution visualization relates activities, dependencies and observed state transitions; a dependency edge or resource wait remains owned by the native scheduler. Execution snapshot and timeline flows traces the read-only projection, interval analysis, event-driven refresh, cache and disclosure lifecycle, including the limits of its live observation clock.

Operations submitted in the same runtime batch share an expandable activity group; explicit Shell Parallel calls use the same display. Single operations remain individual rows, and Shell Sequence retains its ordered group. Group summaries distinguish observed overlap from sequential execution and expose capacity waits and failures. Elapsed time measures the group wall-clock span, not the sum of child durations. Successful groups collapse on completion unless the user chose their expansion state; child command/output inspectors remain available. New history snapshots retain batch membership for reload; older snapshots without that identity keep their original ungrouped presentation.

Recorded timing

performance_timing.js owns the shared observational span reducer. Model calls, operations, numbered decisions and explicit parent/batch IDs establish identity. Concrete command process timestamps outrank surrounding adapter timings. A background launch receipt clears adapter duration; native job snapshots supply process start/end when available. Unknown process times remain unavailable. A run-terminal event bounds unfinished presentation spans and labels the missing final receipt; it does not prove every remote process exited. Later terminal job evidence can replace that bound with physical timing.

Group outcomes count leaf evidence, including unstarted steps and explicit nonexecution. A parent receipt alone cannot turn missing or failed children into success. Parallelism is derived from measured interval overlap, with explicit parent identity and cycle protection. A configured admission ceiling does not establish observed concurrency. Claims of sequential completion require complete measurements; missing process timing remains explicit.

Aggregate timing unions intervals to avoid counting parallel work twice within a category and avoids duplicating measured parent/child tool spans. Cached historical unions are rebuilt by revision; local ticks add active spans. A known total produces an unattributed remainder only when terminal measurements are complete. Recorded response breakdowns can distinguish Thought, Executed, their overlap and Waited/overhead. Incomplete breakdowns label unmeasured time, while legacy cumulative aggregates stay partial instead of being subtracted to invent waiting.

Model rejection details retain bounded, allowlisted scalar diagnostics and prefer a specific causal explanation over a later generic rejection. They omit arbitrary provider metadata. The supplied 200 ms ticker performs local rendering only; visibility, enabling and disposal belong to its caller. Focused reducer and browser contracts are in test_performance_timing.py and test_performance_timing_playwright.py.

Durable task and request lifetime

The backend keeps a separate compact timing record for whole-task and single-request footers. observability/task_timing.py reduces events at trace ingestion, before persistence. It retains lifecycle changes, call/operation/job identities and timestamp boundaries rather than command bodies. Repeated operations and repeated capacity waits retain separate visits; duplicate terminal receipts do not add the same interval again. Invalid timestamps or missing identity leave coverage unknown.

tasks/timing.py combines those compact headers with task lifecycle and all attempts, independently of the visible history page. It clips intervals to the task's lifetime and counts each elapsed millisecond in one category. These are wall-time observations, not CPU utilization or a measurement of the model's internal reasoning.

Category Attribution
overlap Thinking and execution are both observed in the same interval
thinking Model request/response work is observed, with no simultaneous execution
execution Tool/process/job work is observed, with no simultaneous thinking
unmeasured Coverage is missing or inconsistent and no measured thinking/execution takes priority
waiting A lifecycle, capacity, dependency or user-response wait covers the interval
active Known active lifecycle time remains without a more specific category

The table follows attribution priority. For example, measured background execution continues to count while the request waits for that job. Multiple parallel commands are counted once as execution; a launch wrapper does not add another execution span. A model call cancelled before obtaining a slot remains waiting. Missing terminal receipts become unmeasured when bounded by request completion; detached command evidence cannot prove subsequent execution duration.

A whole-task total starts at task creation and can include queueing, pauses, retries and gaps before a verified continuation. Reopening a terminal task preserves that gap as waiting and uses its latest terminal boundary. A request-only projection starts at that request's own boundary and excludes ancestors and gaps between requests. It returns no breakdown when compact receipt state is unavailable; a settled partial request does not keep advancing its request-only clock.

tasks/timing_store.py records task create/status transitions in the owner's transaction. Standalone SQL uses triggers; RAM uses the task-record change hook. Recovery/checkpoint serialization disables the SQL triggers and does not backfill missing historical observations. Deletion removes timing rows, and late cache writes cannot recreate a retired task.

TaskTimingProjector reads compact headers through the trace owner without restoring or replaying event journals. Its cache signature covers selected task/attempt boundaries and receipt revisions. An unchanged running projection adds nonnegative elapsed time only to its current category; finished totals stay fixed. Changed source signatures rebuild the breakdown. Compact lane reads use persist=False, so they can compute timing without writing a derived cache. Task and trace repositories are read separately; a subsequent changed signature incorporates newer observations.

Timing fixtures cover interval unions, reopened tasks, missing receipts, repeated operations, cache invalidation and SQL/RAM recovery. The API fixture checks that different history page sizes and compact lane reads return the same whole-task total without hydrating full traces. Browser rendering remains described in UI timing scopes.

Activity and model diagnostics

The desktop activity inspector and dedicated mobile lazy trace panel consume server projections. Reload/reconnect rebuilds the view from available server data. Do not infer that a closed tab cancels a server process, or that a visible completed tool proves the entire run's contract has been satisfied.

Source owners: observability/agent_trace.py, native event/publication/progress modules, desktop activity/execution-visualization modules, and mobile/lazy/trace_details.js.

Model request diagnostics distinguish normal execution configuration from internal phase policy. Execution traces report the profile/version, configured catalog names, configured/omitted counts and output reservation. They do not fabricate a temperature or provider output limit for omitted fields. Stop strings and expert-map contents are excluded from these diagnostics. A reservation is a context-budget fact, not proof that an output limit was sent. Provider rejections can identify configured controls without recording raw provider error text or changing saved settings.

Interrupted native streams retain the lifecycle native_stream_error (or native_stream_incomplete) independently of provider_diagnostic.category. Transport categories reuse the provider classifier; SSE decoding, parsing and size-limit failures have stable stream categories. Monotonic first-event latency, largest accepted-event gap, idle time at failure and a bounded failure-stage code join configured/effective timing limits in the existing diagnostic allowlist. No raw stream chunks, hidden reasoning or arguments are added. Compact conversation history retains these safe diagnostics and centralized error copy, so replay uses the same causal heading as live activity. Historical records without a cause show “Model response was interrupted”. None of these facts authorize partial output or trigger a replacement inference.

execution.command.resource_wait records the initial admission wait and material blocker changes, without per-poll trace events. Desktop/mobile show Waiting for resource · Not started. execution.command.resource_admitted clears that wait when admission succeeds. Attention escalation carries backend-derived reason, waiting age, liveness, revision and eligible actions; raw foreign commands, environments and logs are excluded. Claim history records stale foreground repair; resource decision and continuation events record acceptance and zero recovery model calls. Execution bookkeeping timestamps and material fingerprints do not count as new observed command output in progress/convergence accounting.

Disabled-check observations and capability history

The optional Monitor disabled Agent Checks preference adds agent_check.observed to ordinary Activity. Each informational row identifies the check, states that execution continued because enforcement is disabled, and offers Learn more through the shared Manual link resolver. These events contain bounded catalog identities and allowlisted numeric/boolean facts, never raw commands, prompts, paths or tool arguments. They do not become tool results or model messages.

Every durable capability event, including selection started/completed/failed, remains a separate chronological Activity entry on desktop and mobile, live and after reload. The existing capability outbox and trace journal remain authoritative. Replay is deduplicated by capability_event_id; distinct events are not merged by type. Unknown future capability families receive a generic Activity row. Passive observations similarly use agent_check_observation_id and the existing journal, without another event store or user-facing log.

Research failures and continuation

Activities classify actual authority/policy denials as policy rejections. executed=false alone is not a policy decision: invalid research references, soft allowance exhaustion, protocol failures and remote access failures retain their own causes. Execution true, false and unknown remain distinct. Live, restored and mobile views retain operation, acquisition and error-occurrence identities without page content. Repeated failures with the same error kind remain separate occurrences. The Browser privacy latch preserves only allowlisted identities, catalog causes and execution facts in diagnostics.

Research allowance requests reuse the authority card and reply transaction. Reload shows the same exact increments and request ID; approval and denial resume the same run without an extra grant-prompt model call. Completion rejection and correction failures retain the original causal reason. Incidental prose discarded during the single research correction is a bounded diagnostic event, never an accepted answer.

Document research emits distinct web_research.document.discovered, .acquired, .inspected and .images_presented events. Static access failures use web_research.source.blocked; existing Browser operations retain their own trace. Entity resolution uses web_research.entity.unresolved, .clarification_requested and .clarification_resolved; web_research.contract.frozen records the new revision. Desktop and mobile Activity retain these notices after reload, along with existing completion validation records. Structural metadata includes bounded source/entity IDs, page numbers, byte counts, operation names and materialization truth. It includes no document body, private path, binary image or hidden reasoning. Type/provenance failures retain their catalog cause and are not relabeled as policy denials.

Compact conversation reads

Desktop and dedicated mobile share one selected-conversation snapshot owner. A known conversation deep link reads /api/agent/conversations/{id}/snapshot and one bounded turn page. The snapshot contains conversation metadata, normalized task relationships, current execution controls, server timing, a trace generation/cursor and execution observation. Composer catalogs, permissions, attachments and other optional panels load after current execution state. No current-run discovery is necessary for a known ID.

The owner coalesces in-flight reads, aborts on navigation and checks the navigation generation before applying a response. A committed invalidation arriving during a read causes one trailing reconciliation. Reconnect preserves the last coherent status and server-based elapsed time, with connection freshness displayed separately. Previously active request IDs remain in the next reconciliation so completion is not lost when the queue advances. Native terminal truth does not wait for the last trace frame; the final answer is a separate retained read. Revisions suppress redundant application, not updates to durable state. Snapshots use Cache-Control: no-store.

AgentTraceStore has three read tiers: header/status/timing; bounded cursor windows; and explicit full trace/export. Routine snapshots, compact native/lane reads and Shell heartbeats use zero get_trace calls. Delta windows pair generation, cursor and terminal state in one read and drain retained events before closing. Idle trace, command and UI invalidation streams wait on cancellable async notifications from the existing writers; they do not occupy the API worker pool or add a polling loop. Disconnect removes the listener immediately. Capture retention and execution lifetime do not depend on listeners.

A projection scope captures live redaction policy once. Nested field/event projections reuse it, while explicit source policy overrides keep their established semantics. Each SSE batch ends its scope before yielding. Turning optional redaction off still preserves literal permitted evidence; execution and completion continue to use raw receipts.

Bounded Activity history

Opening Activity loads at most 100 presentation events from the retained cursor window. Older/Newer controls replace that page and dispose its viewers. At most 125 live rows plus 100 historical rows remain mounted. Removed rows remain accessible through retained history. Only explicitly cumulative model-progress updates for the same call/operation/ phase are grouped; waits, errors, messages and distinct results remain separate. “Show exact event sequence” disables grouping, and each row links to its full retained event. Legacy chat-only visualization snapshots have the same bounded paging adapter.

Shell transcript chunks remain on the existing command inspector stream. An unopened output disclosure creates no output transport. Closing a page/disclosure disposes its viewer without cancelling the underlying operation. Current execution state never waits for historical Activity reconstruction, including when the Activity preference is open.

Release budgets: at most three critical JSON reads; zero duplicate authoritative GETs in flight per owner/key; one policy-provider read per projection; zero full-trace copies on compact paths; lane ≤16 KiB for one task and ≤192 KiB for 100; native status ≤32 KiB; first Activity page ≤128 KiB and mounted rows ≤250. Warm localhost p95 gates are 750 ms for current state, 1,000 ms for trace readiness, 750 ms for Activity disclosure, 500 ms for a 10k-event snapshot, 100 ms for frame-to-status paint and 100 ms for observation. Open Activity may add at most 150 ms to current-state p95; Activity reconstruction must not create a main-thread task over 100 ms.

Run REFRESH_BENCHMARK=after PYTHONPATH=src:tests .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/e2e/test_instant_refresh_benchmark.py from the repository root. It uses an isolated local server, synthetic retained evidence and 30 warm samples per desktop/mobile case; JSON evidence lives in docs/assets/instant-refresh-hardening/. Deterministic budget and race tests run without the benchmark environment variable.

Supervision evidence and narration

Desktop and mobile show the same retained supervision state, last-check time and observation freshness. An active observation claim can display “Inspecting…” without adding a durable row. Meaningful health transitions use factual activity.supervision.* events. Ordinary observations replace the latest record; they do not append heartbeat history. Attached completion probes and background status probes add no supervision rows. The execution inspector exposes health, cadence and freshness separately. Completion diagnostics distinguish Gateway finish time, controller terminal observation time, probe counts/failures and health-inspection counts. No probe calls the model.

Existing status surfaces distinguish progress-unknown, actionable attention, recovery and restored waiting. activity.recovery_started, activity.recovery_attempt, and activity.wait_restored record the wake, consumed allowance and restoration reason. Duplicate-incident suppression uses the existing watchdog diagnostic counter. Unresolved attention remains inspectable while waiting resumes; ordinary polls add no narration.

Nonterminal attention uses the existing wake journal. Its model envelope contains at most eight Activities and less than 12 KiB of serialized evidence, with per-Activity log cursors and bounded recent output. Existing optional redaction preferences apply before projection bounds. Current raw execution receipts retain their existing ownership.

An attention continuation may emit ordinary investigative prose. Only the established agent.progress.narration path renders that actual model text. The runtime does not write an assistant sentence, summarize logs with a helper model, or synthesize narration when Generate prose is off. Factual runtime rows remain before the ensuing model prose on desktop, mobile and refreshed Activity history.

Observation, classification, recovery and UI projection make no model calls. Worker metrics_snapshot() exposes due lag and observation/Gateway/persistence duration plus registration, observation, progress, quiet, attention, duplicate suppression, recovery, failure, terminal discovery, transition and model-wake counters. Healthy model wakes must remain zero. Counters are process-local except the retained registration count.
